feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leadership profile. It communicates scope well and shows progressive growth, but it would be sharper with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a focused brand in digital platform modernization, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement signals trust, impact, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and create more room for results.  
- Add more outcome-based impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than measurable achievements. Include outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Minor writing/style issues: inconsistent punctuation in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. mostly no Oxford comma), “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler in Education, and “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—prefer “French (A2, learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive value will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Builds and leads digital governance, analytics, editorial, multimedia, and AI-enabled content systems that improve publishing operations, user experience, and organizational reach.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active, outcome-oriented language like “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading.”
- Use parallel structure in the capability list; “web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences” reads more cleanly.
- Keep the intro focused on strategic scope; leave detailed channel and platform examples to experience and skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely repeats Core Competencies and multiple work-experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure and stronger specificity.
- Prioritize highest-value, recent strengths tied to senior leadership scope and public-sector digital transformation.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy and communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations • Cross-channel digital campaign delivery
- Consider replacing “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Cross-channel digital campaign delivery” for a more active, outcome-oriented phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” closely duplicate the header.
- This section also overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; keep competencies broader and let Topline Skills carry tools/platform detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and easier to scan.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked descriptors.
- Add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail where possible; otherwise keep each project to one crisp line.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent serial-comma treatment.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video series all substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent consulting/NACo roles.
- To avoid redundancy, position this as “Selected Projects” with only the most distinctive examples or details not stated elsewhere.

Possible rewrite:
Selected Recent Projects: AI-enabled legislative search; Drupal 10 campaign microsite; anniversary storytelling campaign with interactive conference display; recurring advocacy video series across web, email, and social.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.

Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the highest-value themes: enterprise web improvement, Drupal campaign delivery, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading enterprise web improvement, campaign platform delivery, and content operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets; keep 4–5 max. Combine systems/workflows/analytics into one impact-oriented bullet and combine governance/usability/channel advice into another.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search engagement, reduced support tickets, or faster content turnaround.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites and modular storytelling components that enabled reusable campaign launches and member resource distribution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects rail; keep one concise mention here and let the project section hold the detail.
- Drupal microsites/storytelling/toolkits also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite” in the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine and tighten web impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, reporting improvements, production volume, or efficiency gains from governance and analytics systems.
- Rephrase weaker bullets to show change: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, bringing advocacy and event video production in-house” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to strengthen decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and in-house capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused, emphasize scope you directly owned, and add any concrete growth/volume metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress ownership and outcomes:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial calendars and content workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing processes to improve consistency, turnaround time and cross-team coordination.
- If available, add metrics such as newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director role’s channel oversight.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and Recent Projects section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially duplicate Core Competencies and the header.

- If space allows, add one proof point in adjacent experience bullets rather than here, e.g. 10,000+ page migration or AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or drop it unless used recently/professionally.
- Consider adding proficiency framing: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal (primary), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages**.
- If space allows, add brief context instead of just names: **Drupal site builds/migrations • WordPress publishing • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages**.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Web Platforms & CMS” is fine, but avoid repeating the same list elsewhere verbatim.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid over-listing it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Implementation Tools** to make the scope clearer and less repetitive.
- Replace broad/dated formatting with a tighter list: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add specificity that reflects recent impact, e.g. **custom front-end components, tag deployment, serverless scripts, CI/CD support** rather than only tool names.
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless other skills also use versioning; it dates the section without adding value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid reintroducing it here unless tied to a distinct tool or outcome.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- Consider adding light functional grouping for scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, replace one or two generic tools with higher-impact specifics (e.g., **approval workflows, intake systems, cross-team planning**) elsewhere in experience bullets rather than expanding this list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid overemphasizing them here.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless collaboration tools are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is currently just a vendor list and misses the scale/ownership implied by your recent NACo and consulting work. It should also avoid repeating “email” too broadly since multi-channel communications is already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show depth, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters)** • **Mailchimp (email campaigns)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and strongest hands-on use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; keep this item platform-focused, not outcome-focused.
- “Engagement” may feel vague alongside “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; consider “Member Engagement” if that’s the real context.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a sharper capabilities list and emphasize methods/tools over broad concepts.

Suggested edit
- Tighten and group for scanability: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting”
- Replace vague nouns like “Dashboarding” with clearer capability phrasing such as “KPI/dashboard reporting” or “performance reporting.”
- Consider swapping “SEO” for a more concrete tool/process if accurate, e.g., “Google Search Console” or “SEO/performance analysis.”
- If space allows elsewhere, move impact to experience bullets rather than here; this section should stay tool-led and concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one strictly tools/platforms.
- “Dashboarding” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content operations, and any concrete outputs or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve multi-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and weekly video content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated in later NACo roles; keep this version focused on initial team/process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast achievement the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific line such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support policy communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support plus the first-podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting tools list, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger, higher-level multimedia claims elsewhere. This item should stay concise and tool-focused, with wording that reinforces current capability without repeating production leadership.

Suggested edit:
